title: oncall-playbook-fallback-choreography
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic on-call playbook draft focused on coordinated fallback choreography for common API failure modes we see most often: request timeouts (edge and runtime), 429s (rate limiting and downstream throttles), degraded streaming (lost frames / stalled chunks), and elevated error rates (5xx spikes). The goal is to give responders a short, prioritized checklist and decision points so we can restore customer-facing traffic quickly and safely.

Audience:
Primarily SRE oncall -> primary responder, with quick handoff guidance for escalations to runtime, routing, and platform teams.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Timeouts: scale fast-path -> check queue/backpressure -> validate KV cache pressure -> temp route to lower-latency variant or reduced max_tokens.
- 429s: identify throttle source (edge vs model vs infra) -> increase rate-limit buckets for high-tier customers when safe -> enable burst override -> engage quota-tier routing.
- Degraded streaming: detect stalled connection vs token emission lag -> restart stream with idempotent resume token or fallback to non-streaming response.
- Elevated error rates: isolate by route/model/region -> rollback recent deploys or switch traffic to last-known-good model variant.

Primary observability checks (first 5 mins):
1) Check Redwood Console - Per-route metrics: p99 latency, error rate, 429/sec, inflight requests.
2) Grafana dashboards: runtime-queue-length, kv-cache-hits, gpu-utilization, host-oom-events.
3) Traces: pick a failed request id from logs (request_id pattern: req-<hex>) -> look for span indicating long wait in runtime queue or failed tensor allocation.
4) Logs: edge proxy (envoy) for 502/504 patterns; runtime logs for OOM / CUDA errors.
5) Pager/Incident Slack channel -> confirm scope: single customer, single route, single region, or global.

Decision matrix (what to do based on scope):
- Single customer, single route: prioritize customer-specific throttles and temporary policy bypass. Create a customer incident and apply a temp rate override.
- Multi-customer, one region: consider regional capacity bump or divert traffic to other region. Communicate via #infra-ops and status page.
- Global, all routes: follow P0 incident playbook (severe). Use fail-open fallback (lower-cost model or cached responses) and engage exec notif.

Step-by-step mitigations per failure mode:
A) Timeouts (edge 504 / runtime timeouts)
- Quick triage (0-3 min): verify if p50->p99 shift (console). If only p99, continue monitoring; if p50 shifted, immediate capacity or routing problem.
- Check queue depth: grafana -> runtime-queue-length > 2x baseline implies batching/backpressure.
- Check continuous batching metrics: excessive batch sizes may be increasing latency—disable large-batch path via feature flag (FF: disable-large-batch).
- Check KV cache hit ratio: if hit_ratio < 60% and we recently invalidated caches, restore cache population (re-enable prefix-caching).
- Temporary mitigations: reduce max_tokens by 30% for affected route via config -> quick command (Console route override). If we have a faster approximate model variant, route 20% of traffic there (canary) -> FF: route-to-fast-variant.
- If OOM or CUDA errors: drain affected hosts and roll pool to next image; create a host drain job (k8s cordon + drain) and engage infra.

B) 429s (rate-limit / downstream throttling)
- Quick triage: are 429s coming from edge (envoy) or runtime? Look at proxy and runtime logs.
- Check global rate limiter metrics: per-api-key qps vs bucket config.
- If edge limiter engaged for a small subset: temporarily bump the bucket for the API key (Console -> API Keys -> Overrides).
- If runtime is issuing 429s due to model-side backpressure: reduce concurrency per-worker (config: runtime.concurrency) or enable burst capacity (Dedicated: add nodes to pool).
- If downstream service (e.g., external embeddings service) is throttling: enable local fallback cache for embeddings and mark calls for retry with exponential backoff.
- Communication: update incident channel with which customers were affected and any temporary overrides applied.

C) Degraded streaming (stalled or partial frames)
- Determine failure mode: upstream chunk delay vs client connection instability. Look at streaming chunk timestamps (console traces store chunk latency).
- If chunk emission stalls at runtime: is KV cache eviction thrashing during streaming? Check kv-cache latencies.
- Short-term fix: switch route to non-streaming mode (complete response in one payload). For chat UX, send a partial placeholder message explaining degraded experience.
- If stalled due to network issues in a region: enable alternative region failover for streaming clients (FF: streaming-region-fallback).
- If client connection resets frequently, consider short-term increase in keepalive settings at the edge ingress.

D) Elevated 5xx error rates
- Slice by model, route, region, and runtime version.
- If correlated with a recent deploy: immediately rollback routing to previous model/version (Console -> Rollouts -> rollback).
- If independent of deploys: check hardware metrics (OOM, driver crashes), and query runtime error traces for common exception (e.g., CUDA driver error, assertion X).
- Mitigation: disable problematic model variant, route to a verified variant, and schedule a hotfix with runtime team.

Escalation & contacts
- Oncall SRE (primary): ping @sre-oncall in Slack and call if P0.
- Runtime lead: Sana Kapoor (pager).
- Infra: Liam O'Connor.
- Product/Support liaison: Asha Patel (for customer comms).

Temporary commands & quick links (common ops):
- Look up recent failed requests: 
  curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN' \n    'https://console.redwood.ai/api/requests?status=5xx&since=10m'
- Check runtime queue: grafana dashboard -> runtime/queue-length (link in incident channel).
- Bump api-key bucket (console): Console -> API Keys -> override -> +50% for key <api-key-id>.
- Route to fallback variant (CLI example):
  redwoodctl traffic split set --route /v1/generate --variants fast:0.2,stable:0.8 --reason "oncall fallback"
- Mark route non-streaming: Console -> Routes -> Edit -> disable streaming

Communication template (post to incident channel / status page):
- Short: "Incident: elevated 504/timeout rates for /v1/generate in us-west-2. Mitigation: reduced max_tokens for affected route and shifted 20% traffic to fast-variant. Investigating root cause; updates every 15m."

Playbook TODOs / Unresolved decisions (notes to self):
- Decide standard conservative % to shift to fallback variants (20% vs 33%). Add auto-canary policy.
- Formalize when to apply per-customer overrides vs account-based throttling. Current practice is ad-hoc.
- Add runbook for multi-region automatic reroute for streaming clients; UX team needs to confirm tolerable latency window.
- Validate the FF names/paths used above with runtime config; some flags are local-only.

Postmortem checklist (after P1/P0 stabilizes):
- Collect sample failed traces (10+) and store them in incident artifact folder.
- Reproduce in staging with load tester using the same token length and concurrency.
- Run a small rollback vs config-change experiment to confirm mitigation effectiveness.
- Update this doc with exact console links and FF names.

Appendix: quick diagnostic indicators (one-liners)
- p50 and p95 stable but p99 spikes -> queue/backpressure or rare heavy requests (inspect batch sizes).
- p50 shifted -> capacity or systemic perf regression.
- sudden 429s at edge with no rate limit config change -> likely downstream runtime saturation or buggy retry storms.
- streaming stalls with normal host cpu/gpu -> network/ingress or client resets.

End notes: this is intentionally terse and operational — keep it near the top of the oncall summary. Add more automations (auto-bump buckets, auto-route to fallback) once we validate safety with canaries.

Document history & provenance:
- Drafted by: Evan Chen (eng-sre)
- Reviewed informally by: Sana Kapoor, Liam O'Connor, Asha Patel
- Related tickets: INF-2345 (timeouts spike), INF-2980 (streaming stalls recurring)
- Next review: schedule for SRE runbook sync (monthly)
